newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-WOUDA CASHES IN ON TOP FORM WITH WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WOUDA CASHES IN ON TOP FORM WITH WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Triple European champion Marcel Wouda cashed in on his superb form in the short-course swimming pool this season with a world record in the men's 400 individual medley on Saturday.

The Dutchman, who just missed out on a medal at last year's Olympic Games but picked up three medley titles at the European sprint championships in December, clocked four minutes 5.59 seconds at a World Cup meeting.
The previous best of 4:06.03 was set by Finland's Jani Sievinen in Lappeenranta in January 1996.
Wouda, who has spent a lot of time training in the United States in recent years, came through strongly in the later stages of the race to hold off Australian Matthew Dunn who took second in 4:05.62.

In addition to a cash bonus of $2,000 for a world record, Wouda has a chance to win a car at the German meeting. The car is given for the best performance of the two-day event, which started on Saturday.
